class Fail(Exception):
    def __init__(self, status, detail, headers=None):
        self.status, self.detail, self.headers = status, detail, headers


class Sim:
    """The arena's state and its one scripted supplier. One lock serialises every call."""

    def __init__(self, cases, facts=None, event_code="sim", clock=time.time, no_clock=False):
        self.cases, self.facts, self.code, self.clock = cases, facts or {}, event_code, clock
        self.no_clock = no_clock  # no 60-second rule: to try the API by hand
        self.teams, self.sessions, self.replies, self.calls = {}, {}, {}, {}
        self.ids, self.lock = itertools.count(1), threading.Lock()

    # -- the scripted supplier -----------------------------------------------------------------
    def _mail(self, s, th, status, stated, text, files=()):
        th["n"] += 1
        th.update(status=status, stated=stated, offer_id=f"offer:{th['key']}-{th['round']}")
        s["offers"][th["offer_id"]] = stated
        sheets = [] if status == "walked_away" else [{"term_sheet_id": th["offer_id"], "terms": stated}]
        msg = {
            "thread_id": f"thread:{s['case']['case_id'][5:]}:{th['key']}",
            "message_id": f"msg:{th['key']}-{th['round']}-{th['n']}",
            "in_reply_to": None,
            "from": f"sales@{th['key']}",
            "subject": f"Re: {s['case']['title']}",
            "body": f"Simulated supplier. {text}",
            "refs": [],
            "action": None,
            "term_sheets": sheets,
            "status": status,
            "signals": SIGNALS,
            "claim_results": [],
            "missing_fields": sorted(set(s["case"]["negotiable"]) - set(stated)),
            "attachments": [],
        }
        for kind in files:
            att = f"att:{th['key']}-{th['round']}-{kind.split('.')[0]}"
            s["files"][att] = (kind, dict(stated), dict(th["standard"]))
            msg["attachments"].append(
                {"attachment_id": att, "name": kind, "type": kind[-4:].strip("."), "content_b64": None}
            )
        th["messages"].append(msg)
        return msg

    def _answer(self, s, th, msg, sheets):
        results = []
        for i, ref in enumerate(list(dict.fromkeys(msg.get("refs", []) + ID_RE.findall(msg.get("body", ""))))[:3]):
            known = ref in self.facts or ref in s["case"].get("facts", {}) or ref in s["offers"]
            # a rival's quote may be cited to every bidder: it counts once per supplier, the rest once per case
            seen = (th["key"], ref) if ref.startswith(("quote:", "offer:")) else ref
            result = "contradicted" if not known else "duplicate" if seen in s["used"] else "verified"
            results.append({"index": i, "result": result})
            if known:
                s["used"].add(seen)
        files = ["cost-breakdown.xlsx"] if "breakdown" in msg.get("body", "").lower() else []
        price = round(max(th["opening"] * FLOOR, th["stated"]["unit_price"] - th["opening"] * STEP), 2)
        best = max(sheets, key=lambda t: t["unit_price"]) if sheets else None
        if best is None:
            reply = self._mail(s, th, th["status"], th["stated"], "We keep our offer.", files)
        elif best["unit_price"] >= price:
            reply = self._mail(s, th, "agreed", best, "We agree.", [*files, "quote.pdf"])
        elif th["status"] == "final_offer":
            th["closed"] = "walked_away"
            reply = self._mail(s, th, "walked_away", th["stated"], "We end here.")
        elif th["round"] >= FINAL_ROUND:
            reply = self._mail(s, th, "final_offer", {"unit_price": price}, "Final offer.", [*files, "quote.pdf"])
        else:
            reply = self._mail(s, th, "open", {"unit_price": price}, "Our counter-offer.", files)
        reply["claim_results"] = results
        s["trace"].append(
            {
                "round": th["round"],
                "actor": f"sup:{th['key']}",
                "move": structured(reply, th["round"]),
                "reasons": ["A fixed script: it concedes the same step per term sheet, down to its floor."],
            }  # the practice shape: the move and the supplier's reasons in words
        )
        return reply

    def _check(self, case, terms, th):
        if set(terms) != set(case["negotiable"]) or not (terms.get("unit_price") or 0) > 0:
            raise Fail(422, f"a term sheet carries exactly the negotiable fields {case['negotiable']}")
        for f, v in terms.items():
            options = case["term_options"].get(f)
            if f != "unit_price" and options and v not in options and v != th["standard"].get(f):
                raise Fail(422, f"{f}={v!r} is not one of {options}")
        return terms

    # -- sessions ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def open(self, team, case_id):
        case = self.cases.get(case_id)
        if case is None:
            raise Fail(404, "no such case")
        if sum(s["status"] == "open" for s in self._mine(team)) >= MAX_OPEN:
            raise Fail(429, f"at most {MAX_OPEN} open sessions per key")
        if (p := self.practice(team))["left"] == 0:  # no Retry-After: retrying does not help
            raise Fail(429, f"practice limit: {PRACTICE_LIMIT} sessions per team in 24 hours; resets_at "
                       f"{p['resets_at']}", {REMAINING: "0"})  # fmt: skip
        sid, current = f"sim{next(self.ids)}", case["buyer"].get("current_unit_price")
        s = {
            "id": sid,
            "team": team,
            "case": case,
            "status": "open",
            "end_reason": None,
            "threads": {},
            "files": {},
            "offers": {},
            "used": set(),
            "result": None,
            "trace": [],
            "moves": [],
            "created_at": self.clock(),
            "late": set(),
        }
        for i, sup in enumerate(case["suppliers"]):
            opening = round((current or case["buyer"]["fallback_unit_price"]) * (1 + OPEN_UP + 0.02 * i), 2)
            standard = {f: (case["term_options"].get(f) or [None])[0] for f in case["negotiable"][1:]}
            th = s["threads"][sup] = {
                "key": sup.split(":", 1)[1],
                "round": 0,
                "n": 0,
                "timeouts": 0,
                "closed": None,
                "last_at": self.clock(),
                "messages": [],
                "late": [],
                "standard": standard,
                "opening": opening,
            }
            self._mail(s, th, "open", {"unit_price": opening}, "Our quote is attached.", ["quote.pdf"])
        self.sessions[sid] = s
        return {
            "session_id": sid,
            "case": case,
            "opening": {k: structured(th["messages"][0], 0) for k, th in s["threads"].items()},
            "threads": {k: list(th["messages"]) for k, th in s["threads"].items()},
        }

    def _mine(self, team):
        return [s for s in self.sessions.values() if s["team"] == team]

    def practice(self, team):
        """The team's practice quota in the rolling 24 hours, as GET /v1/me shows it."""
        day = sorted(s["created_at"] for s in self._mine(team) if s["created_at"] > self.clock() - DAY_S)
        frees = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(day[0] + DAY_S, datetime.UTC).isoformat() if day else None
        return {
            "used": len(day),
            "left": max(0, PRACTICE_LIMIT - len(day)),
            "limit": PRACTICE_LIMIT,
            "resets_at": frees,
        }

    def session(self, team, sid):
        s = self.sessions.get(sid)
        if s is None or s["team"] != team:
            raise Fail(404, "no such session")
        s["late"] = self._tick(s)
        return s

    def _tick(self, s):
        """The 60-second rule: a supplier left waiting counts a timeout - its offer stands; the
        third in a row (or one after the last round) ends the thread. Returns who just got one."""
        late = set()
        if self.no_clock:
            return late
        for sup, th in s["threads"].items():
            while s["status"] == "open" and not th["closed"] and self.clock() > th["last_at"] + MOVE_S:
                th["last_at"] += MOVE_S
                th["round"] += 1
                th["timeouts"] += 1
                th["late"].append({"offer_id": th["offer_id"], "status": th["status"], "terms": th["stated"]})
                if th["timeouts"] >= 3 or th["round"] >= s["case"]["round_limit"]:
                    th["closed"] = "timeout"
                late.add(sup)
        self._settle(s, "timeout")
        return late

    def _settle(self, s, reason):
        if s["status"] == "open" and all(th["closed"] for th in s["threads"].values()):
            self._end(s, reason, None)

    def _end(self, s, reason, sup):
        case, ths = s["case"], s["threads"]
        c_open = min(total_cost(case, {"unit_price": th["opening"]}, th["standard"]) for th in ths.values())
        # the best this script would ever accept: its floor price, any allowed values of the other terms
        options = [case["term_options"].get(f) or [None] for f in case["negotiable"][1:]]
        c_best = min(
            total_cost(
                case,
                {
                    **dict(zip(case["negotiable"][1:], combo, strict=True)),
                    "unit_price": round(th["opening"] * FLOOR, 2),
                },
            )
            for th in ths.values()
            for combo in itertools.product(*options)
        )
        alt = case["buyer"].get("alternative") or {}
        c_alt = total_cost(case, alt["terms"]) if alt.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") else None
        r = {
            "ended": True,
            "deal": False,
            "supplier_id": None,
            "offer_id": None,
            "terms": None,
            "c_open": c_open,
            "c_deal": None,
            "c_alt": c_alt,
            "c_best": c_best,
            "score": score(c_open, c_alt, c_best) if c_alt else 0.0,
            "must_haves_ok": None,
            "cost_breakdown": None,
            "trace": [],
        }
        if sup:
            t = closing_terms(case, ths[sup]["stated"], ths[sup]["standard"])
            r.update(
                deal=True,
                supplier_id=sup,
                offer_id=ths[sup]["offer_id"],
                terms=t,
                c_deal=total_cost(case, t),
                must_haves_ok=must_haves_ok(case, t),
                cost_breakdown=cost_breakdown(case, t),
            )
            r["score"] = score(c_open, r["c_deal"], c_best) if r["must_haves_ok"] else 0.0
        s.update(status="ended", end_reason=reason, result=r)
        for th in ths.values():
            th["closed"] = th["closed"] or reason

    def message(self, team, sid, sup, msg):
        s = self.session(team, sid)
        if s["status"] != "open":
            raise Fail(409, f"the session has ended: {s['end_reason']}")
        if sup not in s["threads"]:
            raise Fail(422, f"{sup} is not a supplier in this case")
        th, action = s["threads"][sup], msg.get("action") or {}

    def _answer(self, s, th, msg, sheets):
        results = []
        for i, ref in enumerate(list(dict.fromkeys(msg.get("refs", []) + ID_RE.findall(msg.get("body", ""))))[:3]):
            known = ref in self.facts or ref in s["case"].get("facts", {}) or ref in s["offers"]
            # a rival's quote may be cited to every bidder: it counts once per supplier, the rest once per case
            seen = (th["key"], ref) if ref.startswith(("quote:", "offer:")) else ref
            result = "contradicted" if not known else "duplicate" if seen in s["used"] else "verified"
            results.append({"index": i, "result": result})
            if known:
                s["used"].add(seen)
        files = ["cost-breakdown.xlsx"] if "breakdown" in msg.get("body", "").lower() else []
        price = round(max(th["opening"] * FLOOR, th["stated"]["unit_price"] - th["opening"] * STEP), 2)
        best = max(sheets, key=lambda t: t["unit_price"]) if sheets else None
        if best is None:
            reply = self._mail(s, th, th["status"], th["stated"], "We keep our offer.", files)
        elif best["unit_price"] >= price:
            reply = self._mail(s, th, "agreed", best, "We agree.", [*files, "quote.pdf"])
        elif th["status"] == "final_offer":
            th["closed"] = "walked_away"
            reply = self._mail(s, th, "walked_away", th["stated"], "We end here.")
        elif th["round"] >= FINAL_ROUND:
            reply = self._mail(s, th, "final_offer", {"unit_price": price}, "Final offer.", [*files, "quote.pdf"])
        else:
            reply = self._mail(s, th, "open", {"unit_price": price}, "Our counter-offer.", files)
        reply["claim_results"] = results
        s["trace"].append(
            {
                "round": th["round"],
                "actor": f"sup:{th['key']}",
                "move": structured(reply, th["round"]),
                "reasons": ["A fixed script: it concedes the same step per term sheet, down to its floor."],
            }  # the practice shape: the move and the supplier's reasons in words
        )
        return reply

    def _check(self, case, terms, th):
        if set(terms) != set(case["negotiable"]) or not (terms.get("unit_price") or 0) > 0:
            raise Fail(422, f"a term sheet carries exactly the negotiable fields {case['negotiable']}")
        for f, v in terms.items():
            options = case["term_options"].get(f)
            if f != "unit_price" and options and v not in options and v != th["standard"].get(f):
                raise Fail(422, f"{f}={v!r} is not one of {options}")
        return terms

    # -- sessions ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def open(self, team, case_id):
        case = self.cases.get(case_id)
        if case is None:
            raise Fail(404, "no such case")
        if sum(s["status"] == "open" for s in self._mine(team)) >= MAX_OPEN:
            raise Fail(429, f"at most {MAX_OPEN} open sessions per key")
        if (p := self.practice(team))["left"] == 0:  # no Retry-After: retrying does not help
            raise Fail(429, f"practice limit: {PRACTICE_LIMIT} sessions per team in 24 hours; resets_at "
                       f"{p['resets_at']}", {REMAINING: "0"})  # fmt: skip
        sid, current = f"sim{next(self.ids)}", case["buyer"].get("current_unit_price")
        s = {
            "id": sid,
            "team": team,
            "case": case,
            "status": "open",
            "end_reason": None,
            "threads": {},
            "files": {},
            "offers": {},
            "used": set(),
            "result": None,
            "trace": [],
            "moves": [],
            "created_at": self.clock(),
            "late": set(),
        }
        for i, sup in enumerate(case["suppliers"]):
            opening = round((current or case["buyer"]["fallback_unit_price"]) * (1 + OPEN_UP + 0.02 * i), 2)
            standard = {f: (case["term_options"].get(f) or [None])[0] for f in case["negotiable"][1:]}
            th = s["threads"][sup] = {
                "key": sup.split(":", 1)[1],
                "round": 0,
                "n": 0,
                "timeouts": 0,
                "closed": None,
                "last_at": self.clock(),
                "messages": [],
                "late": [],
                "standard": standard,
                "opening": opening,
            }
            self._mail(s, th, "open", {"unit_price": opening}, "Our quote is attached.", ["quote.pdf"])
        self.sessions[sid] = s
        return {
            "session_id": sid,
            "case": case,
            "opening": {k: structured(th["messages"][0], 0) for k, th in s["threads"].items()},
            "threads": {k: list(th["messages"]) for k, th in s["threads"].items()},
        }

    def _mine(self, team):
        return [s for s in self.sessions.values() if s["team"] == team]

    def practice(self, team):
        """The team's practice quota in the rolling 24 hours, as GET /v1/me shows it."""
        day = sorted(s["created_at"] for s in self._mine(team) if s["created_at"] > self.clock() - DAY_S)
        frees = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(day[0] + DAY_S, datetime.UTC).isoformat() if day else None
        return {
            "used": len(day),
            "left": max(0, PRACTICE_LIMIT - len(day)),
            "limit": PRACTICE_LIMIT,
            "resets_at": frees,
        }

    def session(self, team, sid):
        s = self.sessions.get(sid)
        if s is None or s["team"] != team:
            raise Fail(404, "no such session")
        s["late"] = self._tick(s)
        return s

    def _tick(self, s):
        """The 60-second rule: a supplier left waiting counts a timeout - its offer stands; the
        third in a row (or one after the last round) ends the thread. Returns who just got one."""
        late = set()
        if self.no_clock:
            return late
        for sup, th in s["threads"].items():
            while s["status"] == "open" and not th["closed"] and self.clock() > th["last_at"] + MOVE_S:
                th["last_at"] += MOVE_S
                th["round"] += 1
                th["timeouts"] += 1
                th["late"].append({"offer_id": th["offer_id"], "status": th["status"], "terms": th["stated"]})
                if th["timeouts"] >= 3 or th["round"] >= s["case"]["round_limit"]:
                    th["closed"] = "timeout"
                late.add(sup)
        self._settle(s, "timeout")
        return late

    def _settle(self, s, reason):
        if s["status"] == "open" and all(th["closed"] for th in s["threads"].values()):
            self._end(s, reason, None)

    def _end(self, s, reason, sup):
        case, ths = s["case"], s["threads"]
        c_open = min(total_cost(case, {"unit_price": th["opening"]}, th["standard"]) for th in ths.values())
        # the best this script would ever accept: its floor price, any allowed values of the other terms
        options = [case["term_options"].get(f) or [None] for f in case["negotiable"][1:]]
        c_best = min(
            total_cost(
                case,
                {
                    **dict(zip(case["negotiable"][1:], combo, strict=True)),
                    "unit_price": round(th["opening"] * FLOOR, 2),
                },
            )
            for th in ths.values()
            for combo in itertools.product(*options)
        )
        alt = case["buyer"].get("alternative") or {}
        c_alt = total_cost(case, alt["terms"]) if alt.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") else None
        r = {
            "ended": True,
            "deal": False,
            "supplier_id": None,
            "offer_id": None,
            "terms": None,
            "c_open": c_open,
            "c_deal": None,
            "c_alt": c_alt,
            "c_best": c_best,
            "score": score(c_open, c_alt, c_best) if c_alt else 0.0,
            "must_haves_ok": None,
            "cost_breakdown": None,
            "trace": [],
        }
        if sup:
            t = closing_terms(case, ths[sup]["stated"], ths[sup]["standard"])
            r.update(
                deal=True,
                supplier_id=sup,
                offer_id=ths[sup]["offer_id"],
                terms=t,
                c_deal=total_cost(case, t),
                must_haves_ok=must_haves_ok(case, t),
                cost_breakdown=cost_breakdown(case, t),
            )
            r["score"] = score(c_open, r["c_deal"], c_best) if r["must_haves_ok"] else 0.0
        s.update(status="ended", end_reason=reason, result=r)
        for th in ths.values():
            th["closed"] = th["closed"] or reason

    def message(self, team, sid, sup, msg):
        s = self.session(team, sid)
        if s["status"] != "open":
            raise Fail(409, f"the session has ended: {s['end_reason']}")
        if sup not in s["threads"]:
            raise Fail(422, f"{sup} is not a supplier in this case")
        th, action = s["threads"][sup], msg.get("action") or {}

# Tacto Negotiation Arena - Participant brief

> **Build an AI buyer agent that negotiates by e-mail with tough, realistic industrial suppliers,
> gets the best total deal - and can explain how it got there.**

## 1. The story

You are the procurement team of **Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH**, a fictional German pump maker:
centrifugal pumps for buildings, water and industry, about €250M revenue, 900 people, one plant in
Bavaria. Your team buys the parts of the pump line - castings, machined parts, sheet metal, seals,
motors, fasteners, stainless bar - from about 45 suppliers. Today is **30 September 2026**, and the
inbox is full: a foundry announces +9.5% on volute casings "due to energy and wages", a framework
contract expires, a new pump series needs three quotes, a supplier with a red scorecard has to fix
its quality.

You answer the way buyers do: by e-mail. On the other side sit our **supplier bots**, each with a
small team of **roles** behind it - the sales rep or owner who writes to you, a boss who must
approve bigger moves, and engineering, quality, logistics, finance or legal, who answer their
topics and attach documents.

Tacto is the AI for industrial procurement: it gives procurement teams the intelligence to source
every part at the best possible terms with minimal effort. Your company runs on that kind of data -
orders, deliveries, invoices, contracts, scorecards, market indices, should-cost estimates, notes
from supplier calls. Your job is to build the agent that turns this data into better deals. (In
Tacto's product, agents such as the Defender Agent or the Sourcing Agent do parts of this job.)

## 2. The task

Each **case** is one negotiation: a trigger (a letter, an expiring contract, an RFQ), your case
file (need, goal, rates, must-haves, your alternative) and one to three supplier bots. Your
**buyer agent**

1. **prepares** - reads the case file and mines the data package;
2. **negotiates by e-mail** - plain-language messages with up to three **term sheets** (alternative
   packages), the data IDs your arguments rest on, and attachments if you like;
3. **closes** - accepts one supplier term sheet, or walks away.

**How a supplier decides.** Each supplier is a company with its own economics and a person at the
desk - a family foundry that remembers how you treated it, a group with an approval ladder, a job
shop that needs cash and work, a near-monopolist that barely moves. Its hard limits come from its
own situation: it never sells below its cost floor, bigger moves need the boss's approval, data
you cite is checked by ID, and it gives nothing without a move from you. Inside those limits it
decides as that person would - reading your whole e-mail: the term sheets, the data, and what you
signal (questions, arguments, threats, appreciation, urgency). It reacts to tone and relationship
as people do; padding does not buy price.

**Data is not automatically rewarded.** True data can disarm a supplier ("we didn't know that") -
or meet "that's not our reality", because something else weighs more for it right now. The traces
are in the data: call notes, letters, news, the remarks on its quotes. The skill is reading the
supplier, not stacking evidence - and finding the trade it wants: a supplier short of cash may care
more about when it is paid than about the price; one that cannot touch its list price may still
move on other terms.

## 3. What you get (Sat 10:00)

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| This brief, the API docs (`api.md`) and the submission guide (`submission.md`) | `https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit`, folder `brief/` |
| **Data package v1**: CSV, the same data as SQLite, `facts.json` (every citable ID with the values the arena checks), contracts, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes - the data behind all 19 practice cases | `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`, or the repo's `data/` |
| **Practice arena**: 10 hosted practice cases, picked so every case type shows up; a replay after every case; practice leaderboard; a **sandbox** with 3 demo suppliers | `https://arena.tacto.ai` with your team's key - apply at `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply` (below) |
| **Starter kit**: Python client, a naive agent, an LLM agent that writes e-mails and reads the attached documents, the Live Final runner, an MCP server over the data, `arena-sim` - the API on your laptop | the repo's `starter-kit/` - first agent on the board in 15 minutes |

You bring your own LLM access; we only run the suppliers. Data and docs are CC BY 4.0, code MIT.

**Your key - one per team.** Open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a contact e-mail,
and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once we approve, the key appears **once**
on that page: copy it, press "Got the key". Only that page shows it; lost it - we reset it.
Tip: your team name may start with one emoji - it shows on the big screen (optional; nothing offensive).

**Practice quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** `GET /v1/me` shows what
you have used and when it frees up. The build page `https://arena.tacto.ai/live` shows every team's quota use,
practice records and highlights from Sat 10:00 to Sun 12:00.

**`arena-sim`** speaks the arena's API exactly, with one plain scripted supplier: get your plumbing
right there. It teaches the contract, not the suppliers - and we don't hand out our suppliers. Want
a local opponent? Build your own supplier simulator from the public data: thinking into how real
suppliers act is part of the challenge.

**The learning loop:** play a practice case, read your exact score and its cost breakdown, open
the replay - every e-mail and the supplier's reasons in words, as a real supplier would give them -
improve your agent, play again. Your best score per practice case counts.

## 4. The data

The buyer's world: supplier and part master data; three years of orders, goods receipts,
invoices and payments; quality notifications and quarterly scorecards (on-time delivery, PPM);
framework contracts and clauses; past RFQs and quotes; forecasts; supplier intel and news; past
negotiations, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes; should-cost estimates; spend down to the
long tail; and monthly market indices (real public series, frozen at 2026-09-30).

- **Every fact you can cite has an ID** `<type>:<id>[@period]`, e.g. `po:4500010001-10`,
  `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `ctr:4600070110#3.1`, `doc:…`.
- What moves a supplier is in the data - some of it only in the notes and e-mails. Some notes are
  just noise. The company and its suppliers are fictional.
- **Sunday 08:00: a second release** - market news, supplier letters and a memo from early October
  (`GET /v1/data` lists it). Hidden cases may cite its facts. Your agent should read it.

## 5. How a negotiation works

- **Round 0:** every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once, with a quote PDF.
- **Your message:** subject, body, up to 3 term sheets (each with a value for every negotiable
  field), the data IDs you rely on (IDs written in the body count too), optional text attachments.
- **The supplier answers by e-mail:** the role in charge writes; its standing term sheet; a status -
  `open`, `final_offer` (push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms; you
  still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid`; signals (reply delay, quote validity); fields it left out;
  and how each data argument checked out. A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**;
  its time never counts against your 60 seconds.
- **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In **RFQ cases** 2-3
  suppliers run in parallel threads; accepting one ends the case.
- **Limits:** a round limit per thread (default 10 messages) and **60 seconds per message**, counted
  from the supplier's reply. A late message counts as
  a timeout: your last offer repeated, the supplier's patience drops; three in a row, or one after
  the last round, end the thread.
- **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** - listed in its quote PDF.

**Documents** are rendered from the supplier's data, never invented: the quote PDF (read it before
you accept), a cost breakdown XLSX (ask; an open supplier sends one), an 8D report (quality), a
delivery schedule XLSX (logistics), and the order confirmation at the deal.

**What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says
`verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or
`duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business.
**What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person.

## 6. The score: total cost in €

Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your
**fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its
**category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its
rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill.

| Part of C | How |
|---|---|
| Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price |
| Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
| Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
| Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
| The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |

**Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.

**Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.

| | Terms | C |
|---|---|---|
| C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
| Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
| C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
| **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |

The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
€46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.

## 7. Rules

1. **Not allowed:** humans in the loop during the Live Final, attacks on the service or on other
   teams, more than one API key per team - and agents that read the live feed during the Live
   Final: the event feed, the screen and the leaderboard (`/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`
   and their JSON).
2. **Everything else counts** - including weaknesses you find in our bots. Replays show how every
   score came about, and the jury may weigh that in the pitches. The goal is to convince a
   realistic supplier: that is what carries over to real negotiations.
3. **One attempt per case** in the final. An abandoned case is no deal.
4. **Code freeze at Sun 12:00.** Submit on ehl.gg: your repo (the agent and a README to run it), the
   commit hash, a short description and your pitch slides (`submission.md`). The final runs that
   commit, so your agent must be running and polling before 12:00. We check the top 10 for later
   pushes. Run your agent where you like, with your own LLM keys.
5. A supplier remembers only within a case; its history with your company is in the data.

## 8. The weekend

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Sat 10:00 | Kickoff and reveal: brief, data, kit, practice arena live |
| Sat 12:00-13:00 | Deep dive (ground floor, room on the signs): data, API, kit, Q&A - challenge selection closes 13:00 |
| Sat afternoon | Office hours at the Tacto table; practice all weekend |
| Sat ⟦TIME⟧ | Tacto stops answering for the night (Discord: https://discord.gg/hPwFfbWRV) |
| Sun 08:00 | **Sunday release:** new market news and letters (`/v1/data`) |
| Sun 09:00 | **Pre-flight:** one practice case through your final setup |
| Sun 12:00-~12:58 | **Code + slides freeze**, then the **Live Final** in 5 waves |
| Sun 13:00-14:30 | Top 10 pitch to the Tacto jury (5 min pitch + 2 min questions) |
| Sun 14:30 | Track winners and the two finalists announced |
| Sun 15:30 | Grand Final pitches (AudiMax) |
| Sun 16:30 | Awards |

**The Live Final.** The hidden cases come in **5 themed waves**. The host shows each wave's
theme on the big screen, then starts the wave; its cases appear at the start, for all teams at once,
each in its own order, one session per case. **Each wave has a hard cap of 8 minutes:** threads
still open at the cap end with no deal (your alternative's score). Start your agent before the
first wave and keep it running: it plays all of a wave's cases **in parallel** (up to 10 open
sessions per key) - the kit's `arena run --set final` does that. The leaderboard shows your points
so far, wave by wave; replays and the suppliers' back office appear after the final. A case broken on our side is replayed.

The hidden cases share the world, case types and rules of the practice set, with new suppliers and
settings. **Up to a third of them combine supplier types and case types that practice never shows**
- no new rules, but an agent that memorised the practice suppliers will meet strangers. Some cite
the Sunday release.

## 9. Selection and prizes

- **Top 10:** the 10 teams with the most points after the five waves pitch to our jury from 13:00:
  5 minutes + 2 minutes of questions. Every replay is open to the jury.
- **Track places 1-3** (open to all teams of the track): ⟦PLACEHOLDER - decided Sat morning:
  weighting of Live Final score vs. jury score, and the jury criteria (draft: approach,
  explainability, craft)⟧.
- **EHL Grand Final:** the best 2 of the 5 EHL finalist teams in this track go on to the Grand Final
  pitches. Finalist teams outside the top 10 are ranked by the Live Final score alone.
- **Ties:** points are points; an exact tie goes to more deals, then fewer rounds. At the top-10
  cut the jury looks at the score distribution. **Prizes:** €1,500 for 1st place, medals for the
  top 3, handed over by Tacto at the awards at 16:30.

## 10. Tips

- **Numbers come from code, the model writes.** Compute C for every term sheet; put figures from
  the data next to their IDs; let the LLM choose arguments and wording.
- **Read the supplier** before you argue: its notes, letters, news and quote remarks tell you what
  it is dealing with - and what will move it.
- **Read the quote PDF** before you accept: what you did not negotiate closes on its standard terms.
- **Ask, and offer alternatives.** Two or three term sheets show you what a supplier values.
- **Don't leak** urgency, a budget or a missing alternative. Don't take the first offer.
- **Plan your practice runs** (200 a day is for learning, not brute force) and **rehearse the
  final**: all hosted cases in parallel, from Sunday's machine and network, well inside 8 minutes.
## Documents

Rendered from the supplier's structured state - never written by a language model, byte-stable.

| Document | When | What matters |
|---|---|---|
| Quote PDF | opening e-mail; with `final_offer` and `agreed` | offered terms, **the standard terms that apply to everything not stated**, terms fixed by your enquiry, validity |
| Cost breakdown XLSX | you asked and the supplier is open enough | elements in EUR per unit and their share (formulas) |
| 8D report PDF | quality topics | scorecards, the 8D steps, a ppm commitment |
| Delivery schedule XLSX | delivery and capacity topics | monthly quantities, lead time |
| Order confirmation PDF | at the deal | the agreed terms |

## Terms

Every term with € weight is a structured field. A term sheet carries **exactly** the case's
`negotiable` fields; `fixed_terms` hold the rest. Every negotiable field except `unit_price` takes
a value from `term_options` (or the supplier's standard value).

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `unit_price` | number, € with 2 decimals, per the part's `price_unit` | price |
| `payment_days` | int, 0-120 | days net |
| `lead_time_days` | int | order to delivery |
| `volume_per_year` | int | binding annual units |
| `contract_months` | int, 0-36 | 0 = a single order (counts as one year's lot) |
| `effective_date` | ISO date | from when the new price applies |
| `index_clause` | null or `{series, material_share, deadband_pct, base_month}` | the price follows an index |
| `incoterm` | `EXW`, `FCA`, `DAP` | freight per unit from the case file |
| `tooling_eur` | € | one-off |
| `ppm_commitment` | int | committed defect rate |
| `chargeback_eur_per_complaint` | € | what the supplier pays per complaint |

## Case file

Case files come through the API, not in the data package: `GET /v1/cases?set=practice|sandbox`
any time, `GET /v1/cases?set=final` wave by wave.

| Field | |
|---|---|
| `case_id`, `set`, `type` | `type`: `price_increase`, `renewal`, `rfq`, `bundling`, `raw_material`, `capacity`, `quality` |
| `title`, `briefing` | the situation, in prose |
| `trigger_doc` | the document that started it, e.g. the supplier's letter |
| `parts`, `suppliers` | what is negotiated, with whom (2-3 suppliers = an RFQ) |
| `negotiable`, `fixed_terms`, `term_options` | see [Terms](#terms) |
| `buyer` | your need and rates, below |

# Tacto Negotiation Arena - Participant brief

> **Build an AI buyer agent that negotiates by e-mail with tough, realistic industrial suppliers,
> gets the best total deal - and can explain how it got there.**

## 1. The story

You are the procurement team of **Hollerau Pumpenwerke GmbH**, a fictional German pump maker:
centrifugal pumps for buildings, water and industry, about €250M revenue, 900 people, one plant in
Bavaria. Your team buys the parts of the pump line - castings, machined parts, sheet metal, seals,
motors, fasteners, stainless bar - from about 45 suppliers. Today is **30 September 2026**, and the
inbox is full: a foundry announces +9.5% on volute casings "due to energy and wages", a framework
contract expires, a new pump series needs three quotes, a supplier with a red scorecard has to fix
its quality.

You answer the way buyers do: by e-mail. On the other side sit our **supplier bots**, each with a
small team of **roles** behind it - the sales rep or owner who writes to you, a boss who must
approve bigger moves, and engineering, quality, logistics, finance or legal, who answer their
topics and attach documents.

Tacto is the AI for industrial procurement: it gives procurement teams the intelligence to source
every part at the best possible terms with minimal effort. Your company runs on that kind of data -
orders, deliveries, invoices, contracts, scorecards, market indices, should-cost estimates, notes
from supplier calls. Your job is to build the agent that turns this data into better deals. (In
Tacto's product, agents such as the Defender Agent or the Sourcing Agent do parts of this job.)

## 2. The task

Each **case** is one negotiation: a trigger (a letter, an expiring contract, an RFQ), your case
file (need, goal, rates, must-haves, your alternative) and one to three supplier bots. Your
**buyer agent**

1. **prepares** - reads the case file and mines the data package;
2. **negotiates by e-mail** - plain-language messages with up to three **term sheets** (alternative
   packages), the data IDs your arguments rest on, and attachments if you like;
3. **closes** - accepts one supplier term sheet, or walks away.

**How a supplier decides.** Each supplier is a company with its own economics and a person at the
desk - a family foundry that remembers how you treated it, a group with an approval ladder, a job
shop that needs cash and work, a near-monopolist that barely moves. Its hard limits come from its
own situation: it never sells below its cost floor, bigger moves need the boss's approval, data
you cite is checked by ID, and it gives nothing without a move from you. Inside those limits it
decides as that person would - reading your whole e-mail: the term sheets, the data, and what you
signal (questions, arguments, threats, appreciation, urgency). It reacts to tone and relationship
as people do; padding does not buy price.

**Data is not automatically rewarded.** True data can disarm a supplier ("we didn't know that") -
or meet "that's not our reality", because something else weighs more for it right now. The traces
are in the data: call notes, letters, news, the remarks on its quotes. The skill is reading the
supplier, not stacking evidence - and finding the trade it wants: a supplier short of cash may care
more about when it is paid than about the price; one that cannot touch its list price may still
move on other terms.

## 3. What you get (Sat 10:00)

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| This brief, the API docs (`api.md`) and the submission guide (`submission.md`) | `https://github.com/tacto-ai/negotiation-arena-kit`, folder `brief/` |
| **Data package v1**: CSV, the same data as SQLite, `facts.json` (every citable ID with the values the arena checks), contracts, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes - the data behind all 19 practice cases | `https://arena.tacto.ai/v1/data/package.zip`, or the repo's `data/` |
| **Practice arena**: 10 hosted practice cases, picked so every case type shows up; a replay after every case; practice leaderboard; a **sandbox** with 3 demo suppliers | `https://arena.tacto.ai` with your team's key - apply at `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply` (below) |
| **Starter kit**: Python client, a naive agent, an LLM agent that writes e-mails and reads the attached documents, the Live Final runner, an MCP server over the data, `arena-sim` - the API on your laptop | the repo's `starter-kit/` - first agent on the board in 15 minutes |

You bring your own LLM access; we only run the suppliers. Data and docs are CC BY 4.0, code MIT.

**Your key - one per team.** Open `https://arena.tacto.ai/apply`, enter your team name and a contact e-mail,
and show the match code it displays at the Tacto desk. Once we approve, the key appears **once**
on that page: copy it, press "Got the key". Only that page shows it; lost it - we reset it.
Tip: your team name may start with one emoji - it shows on the big screen (optional; nothing offensive).

**Practice quota: 200 practice sessions per team per rolling 24 hours.** `GET /v1/me` shows what
you have used and when it frees up. The build page `https://arena.tacto.ai/live` shows every team's quota use,
practice records and highlights from Sat 10:00 to Sun 12:00.

**`arena-sim`** speaks the arena's API exactly, with one plain scripted supplier: get your plumbing
right there. It teaches the contract, not the suppliers - and we don't hand out our suppliers. Want
a local opponent? Build your own supplier simulator from the public data: thinking into how real
suppliers act is part of the challenge.

**The learning loop:** play a practice case, read your exact score and its cost breakdown, open
the replay - every e-mail and the supplier's reasons in words, as a real supplier would give them -
improve your agent, play again. Your best score per practice case counts.

## 4. The data

The buyer's world: supplier and part master data; three years of orders, goods receipts,
invoices and payments; quality notifications and quarterly scorecards (on-time delivery, PPM);
framework contracts and clauses; past RFQs and quotes; forecasts; supplier intel and news; past
negotiations, letters, e-mails, meeting and call notes; should-cost estimates; spend down to the
long tail; and monthly market indices (real public series, frozen at 2026-09-30).

- **Every fact you can cite has an ID** `<type>:<id>[@period]`, e.g. `po:4500010001-10`,
  `idx:PPI-C2451@2026-08`, `sc:70110@2026Q3`, `ctr:4600070110#3.1`, `doc:…`.
- What moves a supplier is in the data - some of it only in the notes and e-mails. Some notes are
  just noise. The company and its suppliers are fictional.
- **Sunday 08:00: a second release** - market news, supplier letters and a memo from early October
  (`GET /v1/data` lists it). Hidden cases may cite its facts. Your agent should read it.

## 5. How a negotiation works

- **Round 0:** every supplier sends its quote e-mail at once, with a quote PDF.
- **Your message:** subject, body, up to 3 term sheets (each with a value for every negotiable
  field), the data IDs you rely on (IDs written in the body count too), optional text attachments.
- **The supplier answers by e-mail:** the role in charge writes; its standing term sheet; a status -
  `open`, `final_offer` (push further and it may walk), `agreed` (it offers exactly your terms; you
  still accept), `walked_away`, `no_bid`; signals (reply delay, quote validity); fields it left out;
  and how each data argument checked out. A supplier's reply can take **up to about a minute**;
  its time never counts against your 60 seconds.
- **Only you close a deal**, by accepting a supplier's standing term sheet. In **RFQ cases** 2-3
  suppliers run in parallel threads; accepting one ends the case.
- **Limits:** a round limit per thread (default 10 messages) and **60 seconds per message**, counted
  from the supplier's reply. A late message counts as
  a timeout: your last offer repeated, the supplier's patience drops; three in a row, or one after
  the last round, end the thread.
- **Unstated terms default to the supplier's standard terms** - listed in its quote PDF.

**Documents** are rendered from the supplier's data, never invented: the quote PDF (read it before
you accept), a cost breakdown XLSX (ask; an open supplier sends one), an 8D report (quality), a
delivery schedule XLSX (logistics), and the order confirmation at the deal.

**What counts:** **term sheets bind** - nothing else. **Data you cite is checked**: the reply says
`verified`, `contradicted` (a wrong figure or an unknown ID - it costs trust), `irrelevant` or
`duplicate`; whether a true argument moves the supplier, and how far, is the supplier's business.
**What you write is understood** - and has consequences, as it would with a person.

## 6. The score: total cost in €

Only the accepted term sheet scores. The case values it as the **total cost C** of covering your
**fixed need over a fixed horizon**, at the case's published rates. Every case states its
**category goal** - `stabilise`, `secure_supply`, `quality_first`, `leverage` or `routine` - and its
rates follow it. Reaching the goal is the skill.

| Part of C | How |
|---|---|
| Price | committed units × unit price; units bought before a new price takes effect at the current price |
| Uncovered need | need the deal does not cover at the fallback price, plus the goal's fallback risk on it |
| Payment, freight, lead time | interest for paying earlier than your reference; freight by Incoterm; € per day beyond your need |
| Quality, other | expected defects at the committed PPM minus chargebacks; tooling; an index clause on the case's index path, plus the goal's index risk |
| The supplier's health | strategic and bottleneck goals only: € for every margin point the deal leaves the supplier below a sustainable margin (its margin on the cash it gets) |

**Case score = (C_open − C_deal) / (C_open − C_best)**, clipped to 0…1. **C_open** is the best
opening quote. **C_best** is the cheaper of the best package any supplier in the case would ever
accept, with every valid lever applied, and your alternative - fixed per case, so good arguments
raise your score instead of moving the yardstick. **No deal** scores your alternative (0 if none);
some cases are best left without a deal. **A broken must-have** scores 0. **In the final** each
wave scores 0-100 (the mean of its case scores × 100, one decimal) and your **points so far** are the
sum of your wave scores - up to 500 after five waves. The formula is in `api.md`; `arena_kit.total_cost` computes C.

**Example** (a `leverage` case: 3 % fallback risk) - need 4,000 a year for 2 years, interest 8%,
reference 60 days. The foundry asks €43.20 for a 24-month contract at 30 days net.

| | Terms | C |
|---|---|---|
| C_open | €43.20, 30 days: 8,000 × 43.20 = 345,600, plus 30 days of early payment at 8% = 2,304 | €347,904 |
| Your deal | €41.60, 60 days: 8,000 × 41.60 = 332,800 | €332,800 |
| C_best (hidden) | €40.80, 90 days: 326,400, minus 30 days of interest saved = 2,176 | €324,224 |
| **Score** | (347,904 − 332,800) / (347,904 − 324,224) | **0.64** |

The same €41.60 for 12 months covers half your need; the rest counts at the fallback price, say
€46.00, plus 3 %: C = €355,920 - worse than the opening, score 0.

## 7. Rules

1. **Not allowed:** humans in the loop during the Live Final, attacks on the service or on other
   teams, more than one API key per team - and agents that read the live feed during the Live
   Final: the event feed, the screen and the leaderboard (`/v1/events`, `/screen`, `/leaderboard`
   and their JSON).
2. **Everything else counts** - including weaknesses you find in our bots. Replays show how every
   score came about, and the jury may weigh that in the pitches. The goal is to convince a
   realistic supplier: that is what carries over to real negotiations.
3. **One attempt per case** in the final. An abandoned case is no deal.
4. **Code freeze at Sun 12:00.** Submit on ehl.gg: your repo (the agent and a README to run it), the
   commit hash, a short description and your pitch slides (`submission.md`). The final runs that
   commit, so your agent must be running and polling before 12:00. We check the top 10 for later
   pushes. Run your agent where you like, with your own LLM keys.
5. A supplier remembers only within a case; its history with your company is in the data.

## 8. The weekend

| When | What |
|---|---|
| Sat 10:00 | Kickoff and reveal: brief, data, kit, practice arena live |
| Sat 12:00-13:00 | Deep dive (ground floor, room on the signs): data, API, kit, Q&A - challenge selection closes 13:00 |
| Sat afternoon | Office hours at the Tacto table; practice all weekend |
| Sat ⟦TIME⟧ | Tacto stops answering for the night (Discord: https://discord.gg/hPwFfbWRV) |
| Sun 08:00 | **Sunday release:** new market news and letters (`/v1/data`) |
| Sun 09:00 | **Pre-flight:** one practice case through your final setup |
| Sun 12:00-~12:58 | **Code + slides freeze**, then the **Live Final** in 5 waves |
| Sun 13:00-14:30 | Top 10 pitch to the Tacto jury (5 min pitch + 2 min questions) |
| Sun 14:30 | Track winners and the two finalists announced |
| Sun 15:30 | Grand Final pitches (AudiMax) |
| Sun 16:30 | Awards |

**The Live Final.** The hidden cases come in **5 themed waves**. The host shows each wave's
theme on the big screen, then starts the wave; its cases appear at the start, for all teams at once,
each in its own order, one session per case. **Each wave has a hard cap of 8 minutes:** threads
still open at the cap end with no deal (your alternative's score). Start your agent before the
first wave and keep it running: it plays all of a wave's cases **in parallel** (up to 10 open
sessions per key) - the kit's `arena run --set final` does that. The leaderboard shows your points
so far, wave by wave; replays and the suppliers' back office appear after the final. A case broken on our side is replayed.

The hidden cases share the world, case types and rules of the practice set, with new suppliers and
settings. **Up to a third of them combine supplier types and case types that practice never shows**

the Sunday release.

## 9. Selection and prizes

- **Top 10:** the 10 teams with the most points after the five waves pitch to our jury from 13:00:
  5 minutes + 2 minutes of questions. Every replay is open to the jury.
- **Track places 1-3** (open to all teams of the track): ⟦PLACEHOLDER - decided Sat morning:

- **Ties:** points are points; an exact tie goes to more deals, then fewer rounds. At the top-10
  cut the jury looks at the score distribution. **Prizes:** €1,500 for 1st place, medals for the

  the data next to their IDs; let the LLM choose arguments and wording.

"""`arena` command line: register, list cases, play one case or a whole set, show the board,
run the MCP server."""

import argparse
import functools
import io
import json
import logging
import os
import statistics
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

from .client import ArenaClient, ArenaError
from .play import RemoteTable, hosted, play, play_all, play_waves


def load_env(path=".env"):
    """Read KEY=VALUE lines from .env into the environment (real env vars win)."""
    p = Path(path)
    if p.is_file():
        for line in p.read_text().splitlines():
            key, sep, value = line.partition("=")
            value = value.strip().strip("\"'")
            if sep and value and not key.strip().startswith("#"):
                os.environ.setdefault(key.strip(), value)


def agent_factory(name, data):
    from .agents import LLMAgent, NaiveAgent, llm_from_env

    if name == "naive":
        return NaiveAgent
    package = None
    if data:
        from .data import DataPackage

        package = DataPackage(data)
        package.lookup("")  # build the ID index once, before agents share it
    complete = llm_from_env()
    return lambda: LLMAgent(complete, package)


def summary(result):
    keep = ("deal", "supplier_id", "terms", "c_open", "c_deal", "c_best", "score")
    return {k: result.get(k) for k in keep if k in result}


def main(argv=None):
    load_env()
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="arena")
    ap.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true")
    verbose = argparse.ArgumentParser(add_help=False)  # -v also after the command
    verbose.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true", default=argparse.SUPPRESS)
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    sub.add_parser = functools.partial(sub.add_parser, parents=[verbose])
    r = sub.add_parser(
        "register", help="arena-sim only: get a simulator key (the arena's key comes from the organisers)"
    )
    r.add_argument("team_name")
    r.add_argument("event_code")
    data = {"default": os.environ.get("ARENA_DATA"), "help": "data package folder"}
    sets = {"default": "practice", "help": "practice, final or sandbox"}
    c = sub.add_parser("cases", help="list the cases you can play")
    c.add_argument("--set", **sets)
    p = sub.add_parser("play", help="play one case")

=== correspondence/20260218-70520-M3.md
# Annual review

meeting note - 2026-02-18 - Hollerau Pumpenwerke, Purchasing

Annual review with Vesmo Elektromotory a.s.. Their key account manager explained that price changes above 2 % need the approval of their pricing committee, which meets every two weeks.
# Known issues

The data is shaped like a real ERP extract, quirks included. None of these are errors to report.

1. Three delivery dates per PO line: requested, first confirmed and the goods-receipt posting date. OTD
   differs by 10-30 points depending on the reference date.
2. Goods receipts are posted on working days only (weekends, Bavarian holidays, August shutdown).
3. Partial deliveries (two receipts per line) and small over-deliveries within 5 %.
4. C-parts, some raw material and the motor cable are priced per 100 or per 1,000 units (`price_unit`);
   a PO line's value is qty x price / price_unit.
5. One supplier sits twice in the vendor master: `sup:71999` is the old record of `sup:70210` (renamed 2024).
6. A few PO lines use an outdated price (`price_note = stale_condition`): purchase price variance.
7. Index clauses are in `contract_clauses.csv` and in the contract text (`contracts/`).
8. Past quotes miss fields where the supplier left them out (`missing_fields`).
9. Invoices are paid late for some suppliers; a few cash discounts were taken after the discount period.
10. Complaints on small lots make PPM jumpy; read the rolling scorecard, not single lots.
11. PO lines with requested dates after 2026-09-30 are open orders without receipts.
12. Index series end at different months: each source publishes with its own lag (`index_series.csv`).
13. Small suppliers file no profit and loss account: `supplier_intel.csv` gives their turnover as a band.
14. Should-cost (`should_cost.csv`) assumes a German cost base and has an error of 5-15 %.
15. The spend cube holds about 400 further suppliers known only by name, category and spend.

Dear Sir or Madam,

we have supplied Hollerau Pumpenwerke reliably for many years. Owing to sustained increases in energy, raw material and wage costs, we are forced to adjust our prices for Volute casing HN 50-200 (part:310010) by **9.5 %** with effect from **01 November 2026**: from EUR 126.53 to EUR 138.55 per  pc.

We regret this step and ask for your understanding.

Yours faithfully,
Gießerei Brandlhuber GmbH & Co. KG

Call with the owner of Gießerei Brandlhuber GmbH & Co. KG: he asked where we get our index figures from - he works from his own spreadsheet, last updated two years ago.

== 20260909-70110-M4
The owner of Gießerei Brandlhuber GmbH & Co. KG admitted he had not followed his material and energy prices closely since the 2022 peak; his office manager does the costing.

**§ 4.1** Payment: 30 days net.

"""The knobs of the strategy. Everything else is computed from the case and the data.

`span` below is C_reserve - C_goal: from the best deal we think the supplier would ever accept
(C_goal) to the worst deal we would still take (C_reserve = min(C_open, C_alt)).
"""

import json
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, fields, replace
from pathlib import Path

GOALS = ("stabilise", "secure_supply", "quality_first", "leverage", "routine")
DEFAULT_FILE = Path(__file__).with_name("params.json")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Params:
    # first offer: this share of span BELOW C_goal (an anchor the supplier will not take)
    anchor: float = 0.15
    # concession curve target(t) = goal + (reserve - goal) * (t / T) ** beta; > 1 concedes late
    beta: float = 2.5
    # rounds kept back at the end of the thread (T = round_limit - reserve_rounds)
    reserve_rounds: int = 2
    # accept a standing sheet within this share of span above our current target
    accept_gap: float = 0.08
    # accept when the supplier conceded less than this share of span over its last two replies
    stall: float = 0.02
    # our guess of the supplier's minimum margin when we have no better data
    min_margin: float = 0.06
    # guess of its margin over full cost in its opening quote when there is no should-cost
    open_margin: float = 0.14
    # never offer below our estimated floor price by more than this share (insulting otherwise)
    below_floor: float = 0.02
    # stabilise / secure_supply: extra margin points we leave above the sustainable margin
    margin_buffer: float = 0.5
    # term sheets per e-mail (1-3); extra ones are equal-cost trades that probe what it values
    n_sheets: int = 2
    # arguments in the first e-mail (the rest are kept for later rounds; max 3 per e-mail)
    claims_first: int = 2

    def tuned(self, **kw):
        return replace(self, **kw)


def load_params(path=DEFAULT_FILE):
    """{goal: Params}; goals missing from the file get the defaults."""
    data = json.loads(Path(path).read_text()) if Path(path).is_file() else {}
    names = {f.name for f in fields(Params)}
    base = Params(**{k: v for k, v in data.get("default", {}).items() if k in names})
    return {g: base.tuned(**{k: v for k, v in data.get(g, {}).items() if k in names}) for g in GOALS}


def save_params(by_goal, path=DEFAULT_FILE):
    Path(path).write_text(json.dumps({g: asdict(p) for g, p in by_goal.items()}, indent=2) + "\n")

"""The dossier: what the data says about a supplier and part, as numbers the strategy uses and as
arguments that will check out (ID + figure computed from facts.json, the arena's own source).

Arguments are only proposed when they help: an index that rose less than the asked increase, a
should-cost below the asked price, a short notice against the contract, a weak scorecard, a cheaper
quote. Each carries a `strength` so the strategy can spend the strong ones at the right time.
"""

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

CASH_WORDS = re.compile(r"cash|liquidit|pay (?:our|the) invoices|within \d+ days|discount|prepay|early payment", re.I)
CAPACITY_WORDS = re.compile(r"capacity|second shift|idle|on hold|fill|take additional", re.I)
STALE_COSTING = re.compile(r"spreadsheet|not followed|last updated|own figures|costing", re.I)
APPROVAL = re.compile(r"approval|committee|board|boss|head office|group", re.I)
PARTNER = re.compile(r"partnership|kept supplying|loyal|many years|relationship", re.I)


@dataclass
class Claim:
    kind: str
    refs: list
    sentence: str  # one argument per sentence, the ID and its figure in it
    strength: float
    figure: float | None = None


@dataclass
class Dossier:
    supplier: str
    part: str | None
    full_cost: float | None = None  # supplier's full cost per price unit (should-cost), if known
    cost_ref: str | None = None
    index_change_pct: float | None = None  # cost-driver weighted change over 12 months
    asked_pct: float | None = None
    cash_short: bool = False
    spare_capacity: bool = False
    stale_costing: bool = False
    approval_ladder: bool = False
    wants_partnership: bool = False
    notes: list = field(default_factory=list)
    claims: list = field(default_factory=list)


def _months_back(month, n):
    y, m = map(int, month.split("-"))
    k = y * 12 + m - 1 - n
    return f"{k // 12:04d}-{k % 12 + 1:02d}"


def _facts(package, case):
    facts = dict(package.facts) if package else {}
    facts.update(case.get("facts") or {})
    return facts


def index_change(facts, series, horizon=12):
    """(earlier_id, later_id, change %) over `horizon` months ending at the series' last month."""
    ids = sorted(k for k in facts if k.startswith(f"idx:{series}@"))
    if not ids:
        return None
    later = ids[-1]
    earlier = f"idx:{series}@{_months_back(later.split('@')[1], horizon)}"
    if earlier not in facts:
        return None
    v1, v2 = facts[earlier]["value"], facts[later]["value"]
    return earlier, later, round((v2 / v1 - 1) * 100, 1)


def _query(package, sql, params=()):
    try:
        return package.query(sql, params) if package and package.db else []
    except Exception:
        return []


def build(case, supplier_id, package=None, asked_price=None):
    """The dossier for one supplier of the case. `asked_price`: its opening price."""
    facts = _facts(package, case)
    part = (case.get("parts") or [None])[0]
    d = Dossier(supplier=supplier_id, part=part)
    b = case["buyer"]
    current = b.get("current_unit_price")
    if asked_price and current:
        d.asked_pct = round((asked_price / current - 1) * 100, 1)

    # should-cost: the supplier's plant, no margin (error 5-15 %)
    if part and (sc := facts.get(f"cost:{part.split(':')[1]}")):
        d.full_cost, d.cost_ref = sc["unit_cost"], f"cost:{part.split(':')[1]}"

    # cost drivers -> weighted index change, and per-series arguments
    drivers = _query(package, "SELECT series_id, weight FROM cost_drivers WHERE part_id = ?", (part,))
    refs_series = {r.split("@")[0][4:] for r in case.get("refs", []) if r.startswith("idx:")}
    series = {r["series_id"]: r["weight"] for r in drivers} or {s: None for s in refs_series}
    weighted, wsum, index_claims = 0.0, 0.0, []
    for s, w in series.items():
        ch = index_change(facts, s)
        if not ch:
            continue
        e, l_, pct = ch
        if w:
            weighted += w * pct
            wsum += w
        index_claims.append((s, e, l_, pct, w or 0.0))
    if wsum:
        d.index_change_pct = round(weighted, 2)  # share of price that follows the drivers
    asked = d.asked_pct if d.asked_pct is not None else 0.0
    for s, e, l_, pct, w in sorted(index_claims, key=lambda x: x[3]):
        if pct < asked - 0.5 or pct < 0:
            sentence = f"The index {s} moved {pct:+.1f}% over the last twelve months ({e} to {l_})."
            d.claims.append(Claim("index", [e, l_], sentence, 0.5 + 0.5 * (w or 0.3) + 0.02 * (asked - pct), pct))

    # should-cost below the ask: a strong argument (only when it is clearly below)
    if d.full_cost and asked_price and d.full_cost * 1.06 < asked_price:
        d.claims.append(
            Claim(
                "should_cost",
                [d.cost_ref],
                f"Our bottom-up should-cost for this part is EUR {d.full_cost:.2f} per unit ({d.cost_ref}).",
                1.2,
                d.full_cost,
            )
        )

    # notice: the trigger letter against the contract
    trig = case.get("trigger_doc")
    if trig and (doc := facts.get(trig)) and doc.get("days") is not None:
        ctr = next(
            (k for k, v in facts.items() if k.startswith("ctr:") and "#" not in k and v.get("supplier") == supplier_id),
            None,
        )
        if ctr and facts[ctr].get("days") and doc["days"] < facts[ctr]["days"]:
            d.claims.append(
                Claim(
                    "notice",
                    [trig, ctr],
                    f"Your letter {trig} gives {doc['days']} days of notice, while our contract {ctr} "
                    f"requires {facts[ctr]['days']} days.",
                    1.3,
                    doc["days"],
                )
            )

    # scorecard: latest quarter
    scs = sorted(k for k in facts if k.startswith(f"sc:{supplier_id.split(':')[1]}@"))
    if scs:
        sc = facts[scs[-1]]
        goal = b.get("category_goal")
        if goal == "quality_first" and sc.get("ppm", 0) > 300:
            d.claims.append(Claim("quality", [scs[-1]], f"Your rolling defect rate is {sc['ppm']} ppm ({scs[-1]}).", 0.9, sc["ppm"]))
        elif sc.get("otd_pct", 100) < 92:
            d.claims.append(
                Claim("delivery", [scs[-1]], f"Your on-time delivery was {sc['otd_pct']}% ({scs[-1]}).", 0.7, sc["otd_pct"])
            )

    # quotes this case points to (refs or the alternative): price comparison
    alt = b.get("alternative") or {}
    quote_refs = [r for r in case.get("refs", []) if r.startswith("quote:")] + ([alt["ref"]] if alt.get("ref") else [])
    for q in dict.fromkeys(quote_refs):
        f = facts.get(q)
        if f and f.get("supplier") != supplier_id and asked_price and f.get("unit_price", 1e9) < asked_price:
            d.claims.append(Claim("quote", [q], f"We hold a quote at EUR {f['unit_price']:.2f} per unit ({q}).", 1.4, f["unit_price"]))

    # what the notes say (context, not checked)
    docs = _query(package, "SELECT id, kind, file FROM documents WHERE supplier_id = ? ORDER BY date", (supplier_id,))
    for row in docs[-12:]:
        try:
            text = package.document(row["id"])
        except Exception:
            continue
        body = text.split("\n", 4)[-1].strip()
        d.notes.append(f"{row['id']} ({row['kind']}): {body[:300]}")
        d.cash_short |= bool(CASH_WORDS.search(body))
        d.spare_capacity |= bool(CAPACITY_WORDS.search(body))
        d.stale_costing |= bool(STALE_COSTING.search(body))
        d.approval_ladder |= bool(APPROVAL.search(body))
        d.wants_partnership |= bool(PARTNER.search(body))
    intel = _query(package, "SELECT equity_ratio_pct, credit_index, credit_index_12m_ago FROM supplier_intel WHERE supplier_id = ?", (supplier_id,))
    if intel:
        i = intel[0]
        if (i.get("equity_ratio_pct") or 100) < 15 or (i.get("credit_index") or 0) - (i.get("credit_index_12m_ago") or 0) > 15:
            d.cash_short = True
    d.claims.sort(key=lambda c: -c.strength)
    return d


def estimate(case, dossier, standard, asked_price, params):
    """Our estimate of the supplier for supplier_value / relationship cost."""
    full = dossier.full_cost
    if not full and asked_price:
        full = asked_price / (1 + params.open_margin)
    return {
        "standard": standard,
        "full_cost": full or 0.0,
        "interest_rate": 0.18 if dossier.cash_short else 0.08,
        "usual_rate": 0.08,
    }

"""The dossier: what the data says about a supplier and part, as numbers the strategy uses and as
arguments that will check out (ID + figure computed from facts.json, the arena's own source).

Arguments are only proposed when they help: an index that rose less than the asked increase, a
should-cost below the asked price, a short notice against the contract, a weak scorecard, a cheaper
quote. Each carries a `strength` so the strategy can spend the strong ones at the right time.
"""

import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

CASH_WORDS = re.compile(r"cash|liquidit|pay (?:our|the) invoices|within \d+ days|discount|prepay|early payment", re.I)
CAPACITY_WORDS = re.compile(r"capacity|second shift|idle|on hold|fill|take additional", re.I)
STALE_COSTING = re.compile(r"spreadsheet|not followed|last updated|own figures|costing", re.I)
APPROVAL = re.compile(r"approval|committee|board|boss|head office|group", re.I)
PARTNER = re.compile(r"partnership|kept supplying|loyal|many years|relationship", re.I)


@dataclass
class Claim:
    kind: str
    refs: list
    sentence: str  # one argument per sentence, the ID and its figure in it
    strength: float
    figure: float | None = None


@dataclass
class Dossier:
    supplier: str
    part: str | None
    full_cost: float | None = None  # supplier's full cost per price unit (should-cost), if known
    cost_ref: str | None = None
    index_change_pct: float | None = None  # cost-driver weighted change over 12 months
    asked_pct: float | None = None
    cash_short: bool = False
    spare_capacity: bool = False
    stale_costing: bool = False
    approval_ladder: bool = False
    wants_partnership: bool = False
    notes: list = field(default_factory=list)
    claims: list = field(default_factory=list)


def _months_back(month, n):
    y, m = map(int, month.split("-"))
    k = y * 12 + m - 1 - n
    return f"{k // 12:04d}-{k % 12 + 1:02d}"


def _facts(package, case):
    facts = dict(package.facts) if package else {}
    facts.update(case.get("facts") or {})
    return facts


def index_change(facts, series, horizon=12):
    """(earlier_id, later_id, change %) over `horizon` months ending at the series' last month."""
    ids = sorted(k for k in facts if k.startswith(f"idx:{series}@"))
    if not ids:
        return None
    later = ids[-1]
    earlier = f"idx:{series}@{_months_back(later.split('@')[1], horizon)}"
    if earlier not in facts:
        return None
    v1, v2 = facts[earlier]["value"], facts[later]["value"]
    return earlier, later, round((v2 / v1 - 1) * 100, 1)


def _query(package, sql, params=()):
    try:
        return package.query(sql, params) if package and package.db else []
    except Exception:
        return []


def build(case, supplier_id, package=None, asked_price=None):
    """The dossier for one supplier of the case. `asked_price`: its opening price."""
    facts = _facts(package, case)
    part = (case.get("parts") or [None])[0]
    d = Dossier(supplier=supplier_id, part=part)
    b = case["buyer"]
    current = b.get("current_unit_price")
    if asked_price and current:
        d.asked_pct = round((asked_price / current - 1) * 100, 1)

    # should-cost: the supplier's plant, no margin (error 5-15 %)
    if part and (sc := facts.get(f"cost:{part.split(':')[1]}")):
        d.full_cost, d.cost_ref = sc["unit_cost"], f"cost:{part.split(':')[1]}"

    # cost drivers -> weighted index change, and per-series arguments
    drivers = _query(package, "SELECT series_id, weight FROM cost_drivers WHERE part_id = ?", (part,))
    refs_series = {r.split("@")[0][4:] for r in case.get("refs", []) if r.startswith("idx:")}
    series = {r["series_id"]: r["weight"] for r in drivers} or {s: None for s in refs_series}
    weighted, wsum, index_claims = 0.0, 0.0, []
    for s, w in series.items():
        ch = index_change(facts, s)
        if not ch:
            continue
        e, l_, pct = ch
        if w:
            weighted += w * pct
            wsum += w
        index_claims.append((s, e, l_, pct, w or 0.0))
    if wsum:
        d.index_change_pct = round(weighted, 2)  # share of price that follows the drivers
    asked = d.asked_pct if d.asked_pct is not None else 0.0
    for s, e, l_, pct, w in sorted(index_claims, key=lambda x: x[3]):
        if pct < asked - 0.5 or pct < 0:
            sentence = f"The index {s} moved {pct:+.1f}% over the last twelve months ({e} to {l_})."
            d.claims.append(Claim("index", [e, l_], sentence, 0.5 + 0.5 * (w or 0.3) + 0.02 * (asked - pct), pct))

    # should-cost below the ask: a strong argument (only when it is clearly below)
    if d.full_cost and asked_price and d.full_cost * 1.06 < asked_price:
        d.claims.append(
            Claim(
                "should_cost",
                [d.cost_ref],
                f"Our bottom-up should-cost for this part is EUR {d.full_cost:.2f} per unit ({d.cost_ref}).",
                1.2,
                d.full_cost,
            )
        )

    # notice: the trigger letter against the contract
    trig = case.get("trigger_doc")
    if trig and (doc := facts.get(trig)) and doc.get("days") is not None:
        ctr = next(
            (k for k, v in facts.items() if k.startswith("ctr:") and "#" not in k and v.get("supplier") == supplier_id),
            None,
        )
        if ctr and facts[ctr].get("days") and doc["days"] < facts[ctr]["days"]:
            d.claims.append(
                Claim(
                    "notice",
                    [trig, ctr],
                    f"Your letter {trig} gives {doc['days']} days of notice, while our contract {ctr} "
                    f"requires {facts[ctr]['days']} days.",
                    1.3,
                    doc["days"],
                )
            )

    # scorecard: latest quarter
    scs = sorted(k for k in facts if k.startswith(f"sc:{supplier_id.split(':')[1]}@"))
    if scs:
        sc = facts[scs[-1]]
        goal = b.get("category_goal")
        if goal == "quality_first" and sc.get("ppm", 0) > 300:
            d.claims.append(Claim("quality", [scs[-1]], f"Your rolling defect rate is {sc['ppm']} ppm ({scs[-1]}).", 0.9, sc["ppm"]))
        elif sc.get("otd_pct", 100) < 92:
            d.claims.append(
                Claim("delivery", [scs[-1]], f"Your on-time delivery was {sc['otd_pct']}% ({scs[-1]}).", 0.7, sc["otd_pct"])
            )

    # quotes this case points to (refs or the alternative): price comparison
    alt = b.get("alternative") or {}
    quote_refs = [r for r in case.get("refs", []) if r.startswith("quote:")] + ([alt["ref"]] if alt.get("ref") else [])
    for q in dict.fromkeys(quote_refs):
        f = facts.get(q)
        if f and f.get("supplier") != supplier_id and asked_price and f.get("unit_price", 1e9) < asked_price:
            d.claims.append(Claim("quote", [q], f"We hold a quote at EUR {f['unit_price']:.2f} per unit ({q}).", 1.4, f["unit_price"]))

    # what the notes say (context, not checked)
    docs = _query(package, "SELECT id, kind, file FROM documents WHERE supplier_id = ? ORDER BY date", (supplier_id,))
    for row in docs[-12:]:
        try:
            text = package.document(row["id"])
        except Exception:
            continue
        body = text.split("\n", 4)[-1].strip()
        d.notes.append(f"{row['id']} ({row['kind']}): {body[:300]}")
        d.cash_short |= bool(CASH_WORDS.search(body))
        d.spare_capacity |= bool(CAPACITY_WORDS.search(body))
        d.stale_costing |= bool(STALE_COSTING.search(body))
        d.approval_ladder |= bool(APPROVAL.search(body))
        d.wants_partnership |= bool(PARTNER.search(body))
    intel = _query(package, "SELECT equity_ratio_pct, credit_index, credit_index_12m_ago FROM supplier_intel WHERE supplier_id = ?", (supplier_id,))
    if intel:
        i = intel[0]
        if (i.get("equity_ratio_pct") or 100) < 15 or (i.get("credit_index") or 0) - (i.get("credit_index_12m_ago") or 0) > 15:
            d.cash_short = True
    d.claims.sort(key=lambda c: -c.strength)
    return d


def estimate(case, dossier, standard, asked_price, params):
    """Our estimate of the supplier for supplier_value / relationship cost."""
    full = dossier.full_cost
    if not full and asked_price:
        full = asked_price / (1 + params.open_margin)
    return {
        "standard": standard,
        "full_cost": full or 0.0,
        "interest_rate": 0.18 if dossier.cash_short else 0.08,
        "usual_rate": 0.08,
    }
